exercises.prompt: they leave — use the supplied stem lähte- from lähteä (“to leave”)
exercises.explanation: lähteä means “to leave”; lähtevät means “they leave”. The stem lähte- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vät: lähtevät.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Subject (who does it) + verb (what they do)

parts.role: Subject — the people doing the action.
parts.formation: he is already the basic pronoun meaning “they”, so it does not need an ending here.

parts.role: Verb — the action performed by the plural subject.
parts.formation: The exercise supplies the stem lähte-, so no stem-building rule is being tested. Add -vät; this ending shows that the subject is he (“they”). Vowel harmony chooses -vät because the supplied stem uses front vowels ä, ö, or y, or only neutral vowels e and i.

exercises.explanation: The subject is plural: kuva → Kuvat. A plural subject uses ovat, meaning “are”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Plural subject (who or what) + ovat (“are”) + place or state

parts.role: Subject — the people or things that the sentence is about.
parts.formation: Start with kuva. The stem stays unchanged. Add plural -t: kuvat.

parts.role: Verb — connects the plural subject to its place or state.
parts.formation: olla is the dictionary form meaning “to be”. Because the subject means more than one, use the third-person plural form ovat, meaning “they are”.

parts.role: Place or state — tells where the subject is or what its condition is.
parts.formation: kotona is supplied as a complete fixed word meaning “at home”. No place-ending rule is being tested.
